name: Florian Karreth — Karreth Lab
title: Cancer Biology and Molecular Genetics Wet-Lab Research Prospect
description: Dr. Florian Karreth's laboratory at Moffitt Cancer Center conducts experimental cancer research focused on non-coding RNAs, oncogenic signaling, melanoma, and other aspects of tumor biology. The group uses molecular and cellular biology techniques as well as experimental model systems, including mouse models, to investigate mechanisms involved in cancer development and progression. The laboratory explicitly provides a pathway for high-school students interested in research training and instructs them to email Dr. Karreth with a short description of their research interests. Because direct outreach is the student-facing route rather than a separate high-school application, this is an especially strong cold-email biomedical wet-lab prospect.

name: Ana Gomes — Gomes Lab
title: Cancer Metabolism, Aging and Immunology Wet-Lab Research Prospect
description: Dr. Ana Gomes leads an experimental cancer biology laboratory at Moffitt Cancer Center studying the interactions among aging, host physiology, metabolism, immunity, and cancer. The group's research uses approaches including metabolomics, metabolic tracing, whole-genome sequencing, proteomics, mouse models, immunological methods, and single-cell technologies. The laboratory explicitly instructs high-school students, summer students, visiting students, and undergraduate students interested in joining the group to email Dr. Gomes directly with a short description of their research interests. This combination of advanced biomedical wet-lab research and an explicit direct-email route makes the Gomes Lab a particularly strong professor prospect.

name: Kaveh Jorabchi — Jorabchi Research Group
title: Analytical Chemistry and Mass Spectrometry Wet-Lab Research Prospect
description: Professor Kaveh Jorabchi's research group at Georgetown University conducts experimental analytical chemistry research involving mass spectrometry, gas-phase ion generation and reactions, chemical instrumentation, and analytical methods for environmental, biological, and forensic applications. The group's official research page states that it has standing openings for graduate, undergraduate, and high-school researchers and directs interested students to contact Professor Jorabchi for additional information. The combination of explicit high-school eligibility, hands-on experimental chemistry, and direct professor outreach makes this an unusually strong cold-email wet-lab prospect.

name: Hongxiang Liu — Liu Lab
title: Cellular and Molecular Biology Wet-Lab Research Prospect
department: Department of Animal and Dairy Science
description: Professor Hongxiang Liu's experimental research group at the University of Georgia studies cellular and molecular mechanisms related to taste biology and associated questions in animal and biomedical science. The laboratory explicitly addresses undergraduate and high-school students interested in becoming involved in research and encourages motivated students to contact Dr. Liu directly. The lab gives preference to students who can make a substantial commitment, including participation across multiple semesters and significant weekly research time. The laboratory's recruitment information currently indicates that openings may not be available, so this listing should be treated as an availability-dependent cold-email prospect rather than a guaranteed current position.
